keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row. The page (Herzegovina Eyalet, list of kazas tagged "[citation needed]") says the pashaluk "was formed from following kazas: Prijepolje, Pljevlja with Kolašin and Šaranci with Drobnjak, Čajniče, Nevesinje, Nikšić, Ljubinje- Trebinje, Stolac, Počitelj, Blagaj, Mostar, Duvno and half of the county of Konjic which is on southern side of Neretva". Today the area lies in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Serbia; the county unions and circles are the researcher's reading, each kaza drawn as a radius round its seat or as the matching Montenegrin municipality (Nevesinje 15 km, Ljubinje 12 km, Čajniče 12 km, Duvno 18 km, Pljevlja/Prijepolje 30 km, Šavnik and Žabljak for Šaranci with Drobnjak, Kolašin). Area: page silent; the shape resolves to 61 cells (about 15,433 km2). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: Nevesinje, Ljubinje, Čajniče, Šaranci-Drobnjak, Kolašin and Duvno added; the earlier shape had 46 cells; the Herceg Novi cell and the Montenegrin land of 1796 are subtracted] The Herceg Novi cell is subtracted.

ledger.note: 1833: the Herzegovina Eyalet is created for Ali Agha Rizvanbegović as a reward for helping to crush the 1831 revolt of Husein Gradaščević.

certainty.note: A list of kazas with no surveyed frontier; the Montenegrin frontier especially is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no row. One page opened (the budget for a three-shape-or-fewer state is two); the Bosnia Eyalet page covers the 1833 creation from the other side. The infobox lists only the Sanjak of Herzegovina as preceding and succeeding unit; Novi Pazar and Prizren are not mentioned. Wikidata id null (unreachable). Pages not opened: Ali-paša Rizvanbegović. Review fix (2026-11-01): the region was widened to the six kazas the first version left out (Nevesinje, Ljubinje, Čajniče, Šaranci with Drobnjak, Kolašin, Duvno) after a second reading of the page; its kaza list carries a [citation needed] tag, so the extent is soft. The execution year of Ali-paša Rizvanbegović is still not given on the page (it says only that he was executed when the Porte found he was building an independent power base); the Ali-paša Rizvanbegović page was not opened. The Herceg Novi cell (also the Konavle cell) is subtracted from the kaza union, because the Bay of Kotor was Venetian and then Austrian, never part of the pashaluk; the Trebinje circle of 25 km had reached it. The Bjelopavlići and Piperi land that Montenegro gained in 1796 (Danilovgrad and the 25 km circle round 19.1 E, 42.65 N) is subtracted from the Herzegovina kaza union, because the Piperi circle reached over Nikšić and Kolašin (2 cells shared with prince-bishopric-of-montenegro from 1796).
